correctness.rationale: C(s)=2R(s)-I, R=(I+sL)^{-1} has strictly positive off-diagonal Neumann-walk entries and equal diagonal returns. The 2×2 Bloch inverse yields g∞ and gn, each decreasing from 1 to below 1/2, hence unique thresholds. The fixed-sum return Hessian is a strict positive quadratic form with nonzero Bloch polynomial; honeycomb edge-direction symmetry makes it strictly Schur-convex. Lifted winding walks prove finite torus return greater with difference at most q(s)^{2n}; resolvent perturbation around a strong matching proves σ∞∼(2Sε)^{-1/2}. Independently reproduced the exact-rational 45-term bracket 0.41705524440007830<σ0<0.41705524440007831 and sample torus return ordering.
residual_risks: Strict Schur-convexity only claimed on infinite regular honeycomb, not every finite quotient.
